evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, values and planned figures are original. P2 evidence supplies equation, angle, order, symmetry and interference-demand patterns only. No P1 lesson assignment inferred.

questions.prompt: State the double-slit relationship taught in Lesson 9 and identify the quantity represented by x.
A diffraction grating has 500 lines per millimetre. What is its slit spacing d?
A grating has d = 2.00 × 10⁻⁶ m and light has wavelength 600 nm. What is the largest possible order?
One second-order maximum is 25° from the central maximum. What is the angle between the two symmetric second-order maxima?
Light of wavelength 520 nm is incident normally on a diffraction grating with 600 lines per millimetre.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the grating spacing d in metres.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the angle from the central maximum to the second-order maximum.

questions.prompt: The angle between the two symmetric third-order maxima is 74.0° when light of wavelength 480 nm is incident normally on a grating.

figure.purpose: Assess whether the learner halves the angle between symmetric maxima before calculation.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white line diagram showing a central normal, equal third-order rays on both sides, and a 74.0 degree arc between them. Do not label either half-angle or include a formula.
figure.alt_text: Two symmetric third-order rays have an angle of 74.0 degrees between them.

questions.prompt: Coherent light of wavelength 580 nm illuminates a grating with 400 lines per millimetre.

figure.purpose: Assess a mixed interference explanation, possible-order calculation and symmetric pattern interpretation.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white line diagram of several equally spaced grating slits and an unlabeled symmetric fan of possible maxima around a central direction. Do not number orders or reveal how many maxima exist.
figure.alt_text: Coherent light passes through a grating and produces symmetric outgoing directions.
